Header: Helicoverpa assulta syn. Heliothis separate, cape gooseberry budworm, oriental tobacco budworm, tobacco budworm, 烟青虫 in Chinese

Prevention: Choose seedbed far away from the pest bases or cover the seedbeds
Remove old stems and leaves of tobacco and pepper shortly after harvest to reduce pupae
Plant tobacco early (generally in mid-April) to avoid peak occurrence period of tobacco budworm
Till deeply (25-30 cm), then solarize with plastic film for 2 weeks before planting to reduce budworm caterpillars
Plant wheat before and after tobacco over a one year break to reduce tobacco budworm
Monitoring: Monitor from seeding through field stage
Survey 4-5 out of 20 vegetative young plants and look for caterpillars under leaves or at soil cracks by daylight at least twice a week
Young caterpillars are greenish to light brown (5-8mm).
At more than 15 larvae per 100 plants, consider a direct control
Look for chewing holes and destroyed growing points of tobacco and soft stems.
At heavy chewing, leaves look window-like
Older caterpillars of 2-4 cm are brown with a back of white dots and rings of black hairs.
Control action is often too late

Use microsporidian biopesticides ( Vairimorpha necairix from cotton bollworm) to kill budworm caterpillars.
Mix cornmeal and biopesticides spore suspension 1:1, then dry in the sun.
